column1: # TITLE: Novel autophagy inhibitor Lys05 enhances impact of ionizing radiation on human lung cancer cells H1299
# SUMMARY: Autophagy inhibition through small-molecule inhibitors is one of the approaches to increasing the efficiency of radiotherapy of oncological patients. A new inhibitor
column3: with potential to accumulate within lysosomes and to block autophagy has been discovered recently. Several studies have described its chemosensitizing effects
column4: but nothing is known about its impact in the context of ionizing radiation (IR). To investigate the mechanisms underlying its role in radiosensitization we employed radioresistant human non-small cell lung carcinoma cells (H1299
column5: p53-negative) in combination with multiple approaches (cell biology techniques to reveal the phenotypes
column6: and quantitative phosphoproteomics to comprehensively describe Lys05-induced changes in irradiated cells). In the presented study
column7: we report for the first time that Lys05 could be utilized in combination with IR as a promising future strategy in eradication of lung cancer cells.
